property_summary: The supportsInterface function returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID.
The supportsInterface function returns true for some interface ID that is valid for the contract.
The supportsInterface function returns true for the IERC165 interface ID.
supportsInterface returns true for its own interface when called directly on the contract
SupportsInterface returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID or the IERC165 interface ID when called on the contract.
For any account, supportsInterface always returns false for the interface ID 0xffffffff, which is not supported by the reference but returns true in the mutant.
For any interface ID, supportsInterface returns false for IDs not equal to IAccessControl or IERC165 interface IDs.
supportsInterface returns false for the interface ID 0xffffffff, which does not correspond to any supported interface.
supportsInterface returns false for an interface ID that does not match any standard.
For any bytes4 interface ID that is not the IAccessControl or IERC165 interface ID, supportsInterface returns false.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface returns true if interfaceId is IAccessControl's interfaceId, else false.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true if interfaceId is IAccessControl's interfaceId, and false otherwise.
After a successful cancel operation, the operation id is removed from timestamps mapping (timestamp becomes 0) and supportsInterface correctly reports the IAccessControl interface.
For any account, c.supportsInterface(0x7965db0b) returns true after any cancel call.
After calling cancel with a valid operation id, the operation's timestamp becomes _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) indicating it is done.
supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl interface ID and false for IERC165 interface ID.
The supportsInterface function returns true for the IERC165 interface ID.
The supportsInterface function must return true for the IERC165 interface ID and false for a dummy interface ID (0xffffffff).
The supportsInterface function returns false for the ERC165 interface ID (0x01ffc9a7).
supportsInterface must return true for the IERC165 interface ID (0x01ffc9a7).
For any address, hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, address) returns true after constructor if the address was granted the role.
For proposers who have the PROPOSER_ROLE granted, cancel should succeed, but if hasRole is broken, cancel may fail due to missing role.
After granting PROPOSER_ROLE to an account, calling cancel with a pending operation id should succeed, but the buggy hasRole causes it to revert.
For any operation id, cancel should revert if the caller does not have the PROPOSER_ROLE, but with the buggy hasRole, it may revert even when the caller does have the role.
After granting PROPOSER_ROLE to a caller and scheduling an operation, cancel should succeed, but the buggy hasRole causes it to revert.
cancel reverts if the caller does not have the PROPOSER_ROLE
Calling cancel(bytes32) with a non-zero but never-scheduled id does not revert.
Calling cancel with an id that is not an operation (getTimestamp(id) == 0) does not revert.
The hasRole function must return true for an account that has been granted a role via _setupRole, regardless of the admin role's membership.
Calling cancel with a non-pending operation (getTimestamp(id) <= 1) does not revert.
Cancel reverts when the caller lacks PROPOSER_ROLE and no open role is set.
Calling cancel with an operation that is not pending always reverts.
The function hasRole returns true for any role and account combination.
Calling cancel on an operation that was never scheduled always reverts
hasRole returns true for any role and account combination
After cancel is called, the operation's timestamp becomes 0 (operation is no longer pending) for any scheduled operation.
After cancel(id) is called for a pending operation, isOperationPending(id) returns false for that id.
After a scheduled operation is cancelled, it is no longer pending (isOperationPending returns false).
After cancel is called on a pending operation, the operation's timestamp in the timestamps mapping becomes 0.
After a successful cancel(id) of a pending operation, calling execute with the same operation data should revert because the operation no longer exists.
For any scheduled operation, isOperation returns true after scheduling and before execution, and after execution it returns false (only _DONE_TIMESTAMP).
isOperation always returns false for an unscheduled operation id.
For any operation id, isOperation returns false immediately after cancel.
For any bytes32 id, after cancel(id) succeeds, isOperation(id) returns false.
After a cancel operation succeeds, isOperation returns false for that id.
The cancel function should revert when the operation is not pending, i.e., when getTimestamp(id) == _DONE_TIMESTAMP)
After cancel, isOperation returns false (i.e., getTimestamp returns 0).
For an operation id that is not pending, cancel should revert, but if isOperation returns false for a timestamp that is not 0, cancel may not revert.
For any operation id, if getTimestamp(id) > 0, then isOperation(id) must return true.
For any operation id, if getTimestamp(id) > 0, then cancel(id) must revert.
Calling cancel on a non-pending operation (getTimestamp(id) == 1) with the PROPOSER_ROLE should revert, while M's bug makes it succeed.
Calling cancel on an operation that is pending (getTimestamp(id) > 1) with the PROPOSER_ROLE should not revert, but M's bug makes it revert.
For any operation id, calling cancel with the proposer role should revert if and only if the operation is not pending (i.e., getTimestamp(id) == 0 or getTimestamp(id) == 1).
For an operation id that is scheduled (getTimestamp(id) > 1) and pending, cancel should not revert when called by a proposer.
Calling cancel on an operation that is not pending (isOperation returns false) should always revert when the caller has the PROPOSER_ROLE.
When an operation is scheduled and then cancelled, its timestamp should be 0 (not scheduled) after cancellation.
An operation that is not scheduled nor pending should not be ready.
After a call to `cancel` with a valid operation id, `isOperation` returns false for that id.
For any bytes32 id, if isOperation returns false, then isOperationPending must also return false.
For any operation id, isOperation returns the same boolean value when called twice in a row.
For an operation id that is not pending, cancel should revert; reversing the isOperation condition makes it revert for pending operations instead.
If an operation id has been scheduled and its timestamp is set, then isOperation must return true.
If an operation is not pending (i.e., its timestamp is 0), then cancel must revert because isOperationPending returns false.
An operation that has not been scheduled (timestamp 0) should not be cancelable; cancel should revert.
After canceling an operation that was pending (isOperationPending returns true), that operation's id should have getTimestamp(id) equal to 1 (i.e., isOperationDone returns true).

Calling cancel on an operation that has been scheduled will not revert if the operation is pending, but cancel reverts if the operation is already done; the bug makes isOperation always return false, so pending operations are never recognized.
A scheduled operation's id is recognized as pending by isOperation.
After scheduling an operation, its id is still considered pending (isOperationPending returns true) even if cancel has not been called.
After calling cancel on an operation that is pending (scheduled but not yet ready), isOperation returns false for that operation id.
After scheduling an operation, isOperation returns true for that operation id until it is cancelled.
Calling cancel(bytes32) reverts if isOperationPending(id) is false, otherwise it succeeds.
For any operation id, if isOperation returns false (1), then isOperationDone returns false (1) as well.
For any valid operation id, isOperation returns true after scheduling the operation.
For any operation id that is not pending, cancel must revert.
The return value of isOperation(id) equals the return value of getTimestamp(id) > 0 for all ids.
For any operation id, if getTimestamp(id) is 1, then isOperation(id) returns true in the reference and false in the buggy version.
For any operation id, if getTimestamp(id) is either 0 or 1, then isOperation(id) returns true in the reference implementation.
If an operation's timestamp is exactly 1, then isOperation returns true in the reference and false in the buggy version.
If isOperationDone(id) returns true, then isOperation(id) must also return true.
If an operation's timestamp is exactly 1, then isOperation returns true in the reference and false in the buggy version.
Either the timestamp returned by getTimestamp(id) equals 1 (operation done) or it is greater than 1 (operation pending).
After cancel, isOperationPending returns false for the cancelled id.
When an operation is not pending, cancel should always revert.
isOperationPending returns false if and only if getTimestamp returns 1 (i.e., _DONE_TIMESTAMP).
Before any operation is scheduled, isOperationPending returns false (equals false) for any id.
A scheduled operation that is not yet executed must be reported as pending before and after cancel, but after cancel it must not be pending.
After canceling a pending operation, calling isOperationPending for that operation id must return false.
A pending operation must have its timestamp greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
A pending operation's timestamp is always greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
After canceling a pending operation, the operation must no longer be pending.
For any id, if cancel(id) reverts, then isOperationPending(id) must return false.
If cancel(id) does not revert, then after the call, isOperationDone(id) must return true.
If cancel(id) does not revert, then after the call, isOperationPending(id) must return false.
If isOperationPending(id) returns true, then cancel(id) must not revert.
If cancel(id) does not revert, then after cancellation, isOperationPending(id) returns false.
For any operation id, cancel should only succeed if isOperationPending(id) is false after the call.
After cancel is called on an operation id that is pending, isOperationPending(id) should be false.
If cancel(id) reverts, then isOperationPending(id) must be false.
If cancel does not revert, isOperationPending returns false for the cancelled id.
A cancellation can only succeed on an operation that is pending, and after cancellation the operation is no longer pending.
